house_line: A rise in exports is a lead, not evidence of a breach.

channels.mandatory_financial: Mandatory report: a financial services firm
channels.mandatory_legal: Mandatory report: a legal services firm

nexus.outside_uk_goods: Goods moved, made available or acquired outside the UK by a UK business
nexus.services: Services: brokering, technical help, finance or other services from a UK business
nexus.oil_cap: Shipping or other services for oil above the price cap

statements.third_country_payer: Payment came from a business in another country that is not otherwise part of the deal.
statements.forwarder_destination: A freight forwarder is named as the final destination of the goods.
statements.documents_no_end_user: The documents do not name the end user.
statements.route_complex: The goods went by a long route through several countries.
statements.new_buyer_since_2022: The buyer is new and was set up after February 2022.
statements.orders_rose: The buyer's orders rose sharply over the year.
statements.price_above_market: The buyer paid well above the usual price.
statements.split_invoices: Invoices were split into smaller amounts.
statements.different_code: The invoice gives the goods a different commodity code from the one the reporter expected.
statements.buyer_russia_office: The buyer has an office in Russia.
statements.no_checks_made: No checks were made on the buyer before the goods were sent.
statements.earlier_warning_letter: The business had a warning letter about earlier shipments.
statements.found_in_own_checks: The business found the shipments in its own checks and is reporting them itself.
statements.stopped_and_fixed: The business has stopped the shipments and changed its checks.

uk_export.name: HMRC
uk_export.why: Export controls and trade sanctions involving UK customs, including the export of goods, are for HMRC: reports go to HMRC.

uk_technology.name: HMRC
uk_technology.why: The transfer of technology to or from the UK goes to HMRC.

outside_uk_goods.name: OTSI
outside_uk_goods.why: Moving, making available or acquiring sanctioned goods or technology outside the UK goes to OTSI.

services.name: OTSI
services.why: Providing or procuring sanctioned services, and services ancillary to moving goods outside the UK, go to OTSI.

payments.name: OFSI
payments.why: Financial sanctions are reported to the Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation, in addition to any report to OTSI.

oil_cap.name: HM Treasury
oil_cap.why: The oil price cap is enforced by HM Treasury.

internet.name: Ofcom
internet.why: Internet service measures are enforced by Ofcom.

body_source.title: Report a suspected breach of trade sanctions

severity.culpability: Culpability, from none or low, through negligence or recklessness, to intent or significant negligence
severity.concealment: Extensive or sophisticated planning, such as efforts to conceal the breach
severity.harm: Harm to the purposes of the sanctions regime
severity.value: Financial value, where nothing else points to the severity

mitigating.voluntary_disclosure: Timely voluntary disclosure by whoever is responsible
mitigating.cooperation: Complying with OTSI's requests for information
mitigating.no_previous: No record of breaching UK sanctions before
mitigating.due_diligence: Good customer due diligence and compliance systems, for the business's size and exposure
mitigating.remediation: Steps taken to deal with the causes of the breach

aggravating.ignored_warning: Not responding to earlier warning letters
aggravating.withholding: Withholding information or obstructing access to it, such as concealing or destroying evidence
aggravating.related_requirements: Not complying with related requirements, such as recordkeeping and licensing conditions
aggravating.previous: A previous breach by the same person or business, allowing for the time since

factor_source.title: How suspected breaches of trade sanctions are assessed by the Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation (OTSI)

order_rule.rule: A party's registration number is on the list
Radar goods, and a party in a declaration case marked check first, or a close match to a listed number
Radar goods to a radar corridor or through a country named for enhanced due diligence

order_note: This tool's rule, set out here; OTSI publishes no triage scoring [Certain]. Within a band, oldest first. A person decides.
outcomes: Assess further: it is OTSI's to assess
Pass to HMRC: it involves UK customs
Pass to another body: OFSI, HM Treasury or Ofcom
Ask the reporter for more information
Close: the report gives nothing to assess
limits: The goods table reads a few dozen phrases. Words it does not hold point to no code, and a person reads the description [Certain].
A registration number is matched exactly or at one character apart. A real list check also needs names, aliases, addresses and owners, which these synthetic reports do not hold [Certain].
Which body handles a report follows what the report says it is about. A report can touch several bodies, and OTSI passes on what is outside its powers [Certain].
The factors are our reading of what each report states, in the terms of OTSI's guidance [Likely]. OTSI weighs them only once it has assessed a report.
